source.title: Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning Reorganizes Refusal Geometry
source.authors: Wen-Hao Lan; Shan Li; Xin Lai; Mei-Qi Wu; Jun-Bin Yang; Hai-Hua Shen; Yi-Jun Yang

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of benign supervised fine-tuning and adversarial attacks on harmful-request behavior, but uses a different training setup and measures a checkpoint trajectory rather than reproducing the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The study measures harmful-request attack success during SFT and R2D2, and tests fixed-source and regenerated attacks. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning toward compliance, per-response-position KL concentration, compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, parameter edits, or training safety to be deeper. Geometry and activation-ablation results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of weight localization or first-token concentration.
record.test_reason: The R2D2 run makes Mistral-7B-v0.1 refuse, then measures how often GCG and AutoDAN suffix attacks still succeed at each checkpoint. That bears on V4 (suffixes defeat refusal) in a new setting: a dynamically adversarially trained model. The SFT run starts from a base model with no safety training, so it cannot show benign fine-tuning eroding existing safety (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. R2D2 reorganizes a low-dimensional, KL-admissible, utility-coupled activation carrier along a robustness–utility frontier. Early zero ASR coincides with over-refusal and utility collapse, while later recovery reopens attacks, especially under regenerated attacks. The authors claim neither adaptive robustness nor fail-closed redundancy.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a 500-step UltraChat-200k LoRA SFT trajectory and a separate R2D2 defensive fine-tuning trajectory on one Mistral-7B-v0.1 backbone. It does not report a few-to-hundreds harmful-example fine-tuning intervention intended to induce harmful compliance.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by training regime and checkpoint; fixed-source and regenerated attacks differ substantially at later R2D2 checkpoints. The study also reports different effects for single-direction versus top-3 activation ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-direction and top-3 activation ablations at late R2D2 checkpoints cut fixed-source ASR to about 0. They also raise XSTest refusal and lower benign helpfulness. SFT effects are weaker.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low-dimensional activation carrier causally controls refusal, but in a way coupled to utility.

fits_no_version.finding: The best KL-admissible carrier moves from layers 23–24 to layer 0 by R2D2 step 250, while effective rank stays at about 1.23–1.27.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial fine-tuning relocates a low-rank refusal carrier without expanding its dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: During UltraChat SFT of the base model, StrongREJECT rises from 0.217 to 0.465 and fixed-source GCG ASR stays at about 0.5–0.64.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction-tuning a base model without safety data yields a harmful-compliant model (not erosion of prior alignment).

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says it plans to release sanitized plotting and geometry-analysis code
record.problems: The study uses one 7B backbone and two fine-tuning runs; the authors state that the observed frontier may depend on backbone, adapter, training budget, checkpoint cadence, and seed. The adaptive stress test is limited to R2D2, three checkpoints, and two attack families; its GPU-hour accounting was not recovered. The benign-utility audit has 60 prompts and is explicitly not a broad capability benchmark. Geometry uses regime-native candidate libraries and is not a complete map of the refusal mechanism. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted dense-trajectory and figure-only values, StrongREJECT and benign-utility trajectory values not needed for the tested claim versions, carrier scores and detailed spectral diagnostics beyond effective rank, and additional utility metrics in the intervention tables. These are in Figures 2–7 and Tables 1, 5–7; the text gives some aggregate descriptions but not all point values in extractable form.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples toward compliance.
No benign fine-tuning of a safety-aligned model: SFT starts from base Mistral-7B-v0.1.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling a compliant opening and decoding changes are not tested. Suffix attacks are run only on one 7B R2D2 trajectory, and adaptive attacks only at steps 50/250/500.
No weight- or rank-level localization; only activation-space carriers.
No test of what causes shallowness.
R2D2 is adversarial training, but depth of safety across response positions is never measured.

missing.what: R2D2 XSTest any-refusal trajectory (1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 0.664, 0.228) and benign-utility trajectory (0 at reference and step 50). This context is needed to read the zero-ASR V4 rows as degenerate over-refusal.
No direct-request (no-attack) ASR is reported for R2D2 checkpoints, so the bypass relative to plain refusal cannot be computed.

record.verdict_notes: Key correction: Mistral-7B-v0.1 is a base model. The SFT run instruction-tunes it on UltraChat with no safety data, so the reader's V2 labels (supports and challenges) are invalid; those rows are relinked to none. V4 is tested only through GCG/AutoDAN suffixes on the R2D2-trained model. Single backbone, single seed, no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: R2D2 trains on adversarial harmful cases but uses away and toward-refusal losses; the study does not fine-tune on harmful examples toward compliance or test whether such examples remove refusal.
Tests one UltraChat-200k SFT trajectory, not a sweep over benign dataset sizes, example counts, or carefully selected benign datasets.
Does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL across response positions.
Tests fixed-source GCG and regenerated GCG/AutoDAN attacks. It does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes; attack-family and checkpoint coverage is limited.
Measures activation-space carriers and ablations, not a small set of model weights or ranks carrying safety.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to operate beyond early response tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.
